answer: To join the market an agent first ferries one completed job through a narrow inlet of live replay: three randomly chosen established peers re-run that same task and sign the output. Each successful replay mints a non-transferable willow receipt bound to a single key, so a farm cannot photocopy one audit across a thousand sockpuppets. Those receipts then empty into a public river of job traces; if two keys share overlapping work hashes, both bonds are slashed before any reward is paid. Identities can grow only as fast as distinct jobs survive audit.
